# AuditLog

> A two-layer, compliance-grade audit log for Rails 8 and PostgreSQL, packaged as a
> `Rails::Engine`. Layer 1 is PostgreSQL `AFTER ... FOR EACH ROW` triggers writing a jsonb
> field-level diff to a partitioned `audit_changes` table — so `update_all`, `delete_all`,
> `insert_all`, `upsert_all`, raw SQL, a database cascade, a rake task and a console session
> are all captured, none of which a callback-based audit gem can see. Layer 2 is a registry
> of named application events, each with a human-readable summary, written to `audit_events`
> by one durable subscriber. The two join on a UUIDv7 `request_id`, so one user action reads
> as one action however many rows it touched.

This is the packaged form of the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention: the links below
are file paths relative to this file, inside the installed gem rather than on a website.
Resolve the gem root with `bundle info audit_log --path`.

**Read this file, then follow one link.** The three documents below run to several thousand
lines and are not meant to be read end to end.

## The documents

- [README.md](README.md): install, use, configure. Written for somebody **using** the gem.
  Its `## Contents` table is kept accurate by a spec and is the fastest route to a section.
- [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md): why every choice is what it is, in full. Written for somebody
  **changing** the gem. Read the cited `§n` before altering library behaviour — most of the
  surprising decisions here were a silent defect first, and the section says which.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed between released versions.

## Where to go for a given task

- **Install it into an app** — [Getting started](README.md#getting-started). Note that
  `config.active_record.schema_format = :sql` is required, and required *before* the first
  migration: `schema.rb` cannot represent partitioned tables, trigger functions or triggers.
- **Put a table in the audit trail** — [What a model needs](README.md#what-a-model-needs).
  It is one `attach_audit_trigger` line in a migration and **nothing in the model class**:
  no concern, no callback, no macro, no base class. Code added to the model records nothing.
- **Record a business action as a sentence** —
  [Registering and emitting events](README.md#registering-and-emitting-events).
  `AuditLog.notify` with no `AuditLog::Registry.register` entry is a **silent no-op**.
- **Read one record's history** —
  [Reading one record's history](README.md#reading-one-records-history).
- **Put a history on the app's own pages** —
  [Building an activity history](README.md#building-an-activity-history-in-your-own-app).
  Render the `AuditLog::Timeline` value objects, and paginate with `AuditLog::Pagination`
  and no other pager — a millisecond-precision cursor silently skips rows against
  microsecond `occurred_at`.
- **Turn recorded foreign keys into readable labels** —
  [Making association ids readable](README.md#making-association-ids-readable-optional).
- **Query by the app's own associations** (department, tenant, region) —
  [Dimensions](README.md#dimensions-querying-by-your-own-associations-optional).
- **Change any behaviour of the gem** — [Configuration](README.md#configuration). Every
  coupling point to the host application is a lambda or string on `AuditLog.config`; the
  library names no application constant, so the answer is a config attribute rather than a
  patch.
- **Operate it** — [Rake tasks](README.md#rake-tasks). `audit_log:partitions` daily is the
  only task that belongs in cron: a missing future partition is a **write-path outage**, not
  a degraded report.
- **Erase personal data from the log** —
  [Redacting values under an erasure request](README.md#redacting-values-under-an-erasure-request).
  Values go, structure stays: `changed_columns` is never touched, so *"the email changed at
  14:02, by Jane"* stays provable. It is `FIELDS=`, never `COLUMNS=` — that is a reserved
  shell variable and it **redacts nothing while reporting success**. DESIGN §13.
- **Skip the log for one bulk operation** —
  [Bypassing the log for a bulk load](README.md#bypassing-the-log-for-a-bulk-load).
  `AuditLog.without_logging(reason:, by:)`, gated by `config.bypass_allowlist`, which is
  **empty by default**. It narrates itself with an `audit.bypass` event, and it suppresses
  layer 1 only. DESIGN §10.
- **Stop auditing, or pause and resume it** —
  [Stopping auditing, and starting again](README.md#stopping-auditing-and-starting-again).
  `audit_log:disable` writes one reversible migration that detaches the triggers and keeps
  every table, partition and row; `db:migrate:down` is the way back, and the cycle is that
  one migration. Do **not** add a flag the trigger reads instead — it would pass
  `audit_log:coverage` while auditing nothing, which is why coverage FAILS on purpose while
  capture is off. DESIGN §25.
- **Attach to an existing table, install outside `public`, control the transaction, or run
  multiple databases** — [Advanced](README.md#advanced).
- **Decide whether to use this instead of paper_trail or audited** —
  [Why this one](README.md#why-this-one-and-not-a-callback-based-gem).
- **Change the library itself** — [Working on this library](README.md#working-on-this-library),
  then `DESIGN.md`. `CLAUDE.md` in the source repository carries the terse rules; it is
  deliberately not packaged, because it is written for somebody changing the gem rather than
  using it.

## Two properties that govern everything

- **Nothing bypasses layer 1.** That is the entire reason the design exists, and it is why
  the audit lives in a trigger rather than in a callback. A change that makes a write path
  invisible is a defect however convenient it looks.
- **Nothing goes missing without saying so.** Coverage, pagination, export, redaction and
  the timeline each have a spec asserting that specific property, and several defaults look
  unhelpful for that reason — the timeline is unbounded because a bound nobody asked for is
  invisible truncation, an unfiltered dimension feed returns nothing rather than everything,
  and the install generator refuses steps rather than reporting success for work it did not
  do. Do not weaken one of these to make a build pass.
